sim.script-unreadable: The script could not be read: {detail}
stmt.transaction-control: Transaction control: the console handles it.
stmt.not-transactional: Cannot run inside a transaction; it was not simulated.
note.rolled-back: The scripts ran inside a transaction that was rolled back: nothing was saved.
note.same-locks: While it ran, the simulation took the same locks the real script would take (at most {seconds} s waiting for a lock).
note.no-undo-outside: Consumed sequence numbers are not given back, and an effect outside the database (HTTP, files) cannot be undone.
note.static-only: This database cannot simulate by running the script: what is shown is what it contains and what risks it has, not what it would change.
note.simulate-first: A migration can only be applied after a simulation without errors.
finding.drop-table: Drops a table or schema with all its data.
finding.drop-column: Drops a column and its data.
finding.drop-other: Drops an object: code that uses it will stop working.
finding.delete-no-where: DELETE without WHERE: deletes every row.
finding.update-no-where: UPDATE without WHERE: changes every row.
finding.alter-type: Changes a column type: may rewrite the whole table under an exclusive lock.
finding.set-not-null: Scans the whole table to check for nulls, under an exclusive lock.
finding.add-column-volatile-default: A column with a volatile default rewrites the table.
finding.index-blocks-writes: Creating an index without CONCURRENTLY blocks writes to the table while it is built.
finding.enum-add-value: The new enum value cannot be used in the same transaction that creates it.
finding.copy-program: Runs a command on the database server.
finding.external-effect: Calls something outside the database: a simulation cannot undo that effect.
finding.create-extension: Installs an extension in the database.
finding.alter-table-lock: Takes a lock on the table while it is applied; it waits if a long transaction is open on it.
finding.security-definer: SECURITY DEFINER function: runs with its owner's permissions.
finding.transaction-control: Transaction control (BEGIN / COMMIT…): the console wraps the migration in its own transaction, so it is ignored.
finding.non-transactional: Cannot run inside a transaction: the simulation skips it and, when applied, a failure halfway is not undone.
finding.implicit-commit: In MySQL, DDL commits the current transaction: it cannot be simulated with a rollback or undone if it fails halfway.

cli.help:
migration-console — control the migrations of your databases

Usage:
  migration-console serve                          Start the web console
  migration-console status <env>                   List the migrations and their status
  migration-console simulate <env> [versions…]     Show what the migrations would do (nothing is saved)
  migration-console apply <env> <version> --confirm <version> --user <name>
  migration-console check                          Validate the configuration

Options:
  --config <file>   Configuration (default: $CONSOLE_CONFIG, or ./config.json)
  --lang <lang>     es-ES or en-US (default: $CONSOLE_LANG, or the system language)
  --json            Print JSON
